articles.title: FX option expiries for 26 October 10am New York cut
articles.description: There are a couple of key expiry levels to take note of on the day, as highlighted in bold below. The main one to watch is for EUR/USD at the 1.1200 level, with the strike keeping within 20 pips of the spot price. That could offer a bit of a magnetic pull on price action during the session ahead, especially if trading conditions remain relatively subdued. Besides that, there is also one at the 1.1250 level and together with the one at 1.1200 they could help keep price action more contained between the two levels. That is especially the case as the technicals are showing that near-term price action remains caught in between the key hourly moving averages around 1.1215-20 mostly. And also, downside price action is being defended around the 1.1190-00 region since last week. Meanwhile, topside price action is also limited closer to the 23.6 Fib retracement level of the swing lower from August to October around 1.1254. As such, the expiries today are likely to reinforce those levels unless there are any major headline surprises to shift broader market sentiment and the dollar. As always, the expiries are worth keeping in mind for potential price attraction or containment but broader market drivers and technical levels should still take precedence - particularly with several major central bank decisions coming up this week. For more information on how to use this data, you may refer to this post here and/or refer to the Q&A below. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

Preview: RBNZ set to lift OCR to 3% ahead of election as oil and weak kiwi fuel inflation
articles.description: With a hike close to fully priced, the New Zealand dollar’s reaction is likely to hinge on guidance rather than the move itself, and the risk is asymmetric: a hold would catch markets badly offside and could trigger a sharp kiwi selloff. A hike paired with a clear tightening bias would be the most supportive outcome for the NZD and would push front-end yields higher, while “wait and see” language could see some of the priced peak trimmed. Oil remains the key external driver: further gains in crude linked to the Middle East conflict would feed straight into New Zealand’s fuel-heavy inflation outlook and strengthen the case for more hikes into 2027. AUD/NZD traders also face back-to-back central bank risk, with the RBA expected to hike again on November 3. --- A pause looked likely in September, but rising fuel costs and a sliding kiwi have turned Wednesday’s RBNZ meeting into a near-certain pre-election hike. Summary: Economists and markets expect the RBNZ to raise the OCR by 25bp to 3% on Wednesday, its third straight hike after moves in July and September Expectations for a pause after September have reversed as oil prices surged, the New Zealand dollar weakened and inflation pressures proved sticky Annual CPI eased to 3.7% in the September quarter, below the RBNZ’s 3.9% forecast, but some economists see the December quarter above 4.5% Markets price roughly a 90% chance of a hike and a peak near 3.5% by February; Westpac sees the OCR possibly reaching 4% by September 2027 ASB warns that a hold would likely sink the kiwi, with guidance on further tightening seen as the key market driver The decision is due at 01:00 GMT Wednesday (21:00 ET Tuesday), ahead of New Zealand’s November 7 general election The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is widely expected to raise its Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 3% on Wednesday, delivering a third consecutive hike as rising fuel costs and a weak currency threaten to push inflation further above its target band. The call marks a turnaround from just weeks ago. After the RBNZ lifted the OCR to 2.75% in early September, Governor Anna Breman hinted at a pause, and bank economists were divided on whether October would bring another move. That debate has largely closed. According to interest.co.nz, economists at the country’s major banks now see a hike as almost certain, pointing to the surge in oil prices, further weakness in the New Zealand dollar and persistently sticky price pressures. A Bloomberg survey also found that a majority of economists expect the OCR to rise to 3% this week. Inflation slowed in the third quarter, with annual CPI easing to 3.7% from 4.1% in June and coming in below the RBNZ’s 3.9% forecast. Many analysts expect it to accelerate again in the fourth quarter, however, with some projecting a December quarter reading of around 4.7%, which would leave inflation outside the 1% to 3% target band for longer than the central bank had projected. Markets are positioned accordingly. ASB economists said pricing implies roughly a 90% probability of a 25 basis point increase, with a peak cash rate of around 3.5% expected by February. Westpac sees the tightening cycle running further, with the OCR possibly reaching 4% by September 2027. ASB has also warned that the prospect of hikes has been supporting the New Zealand dollar, and that a decision to hold would likely send the currency lower. The timing adds a political dimension. The meeting falls just 10 days before the November 7 general election, although economists broadly expect the committee to set policy on economic grounds alone. Some argue the bank should go beyond a single move and signal that more tightening is coming, while others expect a short statement that leaves options open. The decision is due at 01:00 GMT on Wednesday (21:00 ET on Tuesday). With a hike largely priced, the tone of the accompanying statement is likely to determine the market reaction. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Bitcoin buyers are fighting back, but sellers aren't finished. Here are the two prices swing traders should watch
articles.description: Bitcoin is approaching an important decision point for swing traders. Sellers have demonstrated their strength, but buyers are showing signs of defending the $80,000 area. The latest investingLive tradeCompass maps two conditional scenarios: bullish above $80,860 and bearish below $79,870. The challenge is distinguishing a temporary rebound from a more durable recovery, or a brief dip from another significant breakdown. Bitcoin tradeCompass: The bullish and bearish levels The tradeCompass identifies two directional thresholds. Traders can use them to prepare for either outcome rather than commit to a prediction. Bullish Bitcoin above $80,860 A sustained move above $80,860 would strengthen the case that Bitcoin's recent stabilization is developing into a more meaningful recovery. The potential bullish profit targets are: The first target at $81,770 represents the initial opportunity to secure a partial profit. The higher targets provide objectives if buying momentum develops into a more substantial swing. Importantly, the bullish threshold has already been tested. On October 25, Binance BTC/USDC traded as high as approximately $80,942 before retreating below $80,860. A subsequent market snapshot around 20:04 UTC showed Bitcoin near $80,453. That brief crossing is not sufficient by itself to establish a confirmed breakout or an executed trade. Traders considering the bullish scenario should reassess whether price can regain and hold above the threshold. Bearish Bitcoin below $79,870 A sustained breakdown below $79,870 would suggest that the latest attempts to establish support have failed, potentially putting sellers back in control. The bearish profit targets are: The first two targets are relatively close to the bearish threshold. The third and fourth require more meaningful downside continuation. A breakdown would become more convincing if Bitcoin struggled to recover above the breached level after initially falling through it. Between $79,870 and $80,860, the tradeCompass remains neutral. This is a decision zone, not a requirement to trade. Neither a failed bullish attempt nor a minor decline inside the zone automatically activates the bearish scenario. Bitcoin sellers have the bigger trend, but buyers are challenging them The recent price action presents an interesting conflict between different trading timeframes. On October 22, Bitcoin experienced renewed selling pressure that undermined an earlier recovery attempt. The accompanying CME Bitcoin futures analysis showed elevated trading participation and a close near the lower end of the session's range. That matters because sellers were not merely pushing prices temporarily lower. They demonstrated an ability to sustain downward pressure during an important session. However, the subsequent price action offers a reason not to become overly committed to the bearish outlook. On October 24, Bitcoin briefly traded down toward $79,133 on Binance BTC/USDC before recovering. That rejection was accompanied by unusually high trading activity in the relevant hourly observation. Additional shorter-term observations on October 25 showed repeated unsuccessful attempts to sustain lower prices and improving intraday lows around the $80,000 to $80,440 region. These developments suggest that buyers are becoming more willing to defend the lower trading area. There is an important distinction, however, between buyers defending support and buyers establishing a new bullish trend. The daily structure still showed bearish characteristics in the October 25 analysis. The shorter-term recovery signals had not overturned that broader weakness. For Bitcoin swing traders, this distinction matters. A convincing move above $80,860 could create an attractive tactical bullish opportunity without necessarily confirming that the broader correction has ended. Likewise, another successful defense around $80,000 does not guarantee that support will hold on the next test. The first profit target matters for more than taking profits One of the most useful principles of the investingLive tradeCompass is that trade management deserves as much attention as the initial direction. For either scenario, traders following the suggested plan can consider two actions after reaching TP1: Take a partial profit on the position. Move the protective stop on the remaining position to the actual entry price. For a bullish trade, that consideration arises at $81,770. For a bearish trade, it arises at $79,630. The purpose is to reduce the remaining exposure while allowing part of the position to participate if a larger move develops. Moving a stop to entry does not guarantee a completely risk-free outcome. Trading costs, spread, slippage and execution conditions can still produce losses. Traders should also establish an appropriate initial protective stop before entering a position. The tradeCompass's opposite activation threshold is not automatically the appropriate stop, and position size should reflect the risk of the actual setup. Why swing traders should avoid repeatedly chasing the same signal The tradeCompass has another principle intended to discourage overtrading. Each published tradeCompass allows a maximum of one completed bullish trade and one completed bearish trade under its suggested discipline. If a trader enters a long position and that trade eventually concludes, the bullish opportunity from this particular publication is considered used, regardless of whether the trade made money, lost money or reached only its first profit target. The same rule applies independently to the bearish scenario. An unfilled order does not count as a completed opportunity, and an open position with a remaining runner is still part of the original trade. The opposite direction can remain available if its conditions subsequently develop, but reversing after a losing trade should not be automatic. This approach encourages selectivity rather than repeatedly entering whenever Bitcoin fluctuates around a familiar price. What could make Bitcoin's next swing more convincing? The bullish and bearish scenarios have different confirmation requirements, but they share an important principle: crossing a level is not the same as sustaining a move beyond it. For bulls, the next improvement would be a renewed move above $80,860 that can hold. Depending on the trader's existing strategy, confirmation might involve a candle closing above the threshold, a successful retest or another independently validated entry signal. For bears, renewed acceptance below $79,870 would indicate that the recovery attempts around $80,000 are failing. The extended targets in both directions should be understood as potential objectives rather than forecasts of imminent moves. For now, the central Bitcoin question is whether buyers can turn their recent defensive activity into sustained upside progress. Above $80,860, the bullish tradeCompass becomes relevant. Below $79,870, the bearish opportunity becomes relevant. Between those levels, patience may be the more useful position. For a fuller explanation of how these conditional scenarios work, read the investingLive guide to using tradeCompass. The Fed may leave interest rates unchanged this week. So why could Bitcoin still move? Bitcoin traders have another important event to watch this week: the US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday, October 28. The Federal Reserve, often called the Fed, influences how expensive it is to borrow money. Higher interest rates can make safer investments, such as government bonds, more attractive compared with riskier assets like Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. But markets often react more to what the Fed says about future interest rates than to the actual decision. What does the market expect? According to an October 20 Reuters survey cited in the analysis, 94 out of 100 economists expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% this Wednesday. The supplied survey also reports that all 100 economists anticipate another rate increase in December. That means leaving rates unchanged in October would not be particularly surprising. What could move Bitcoin is whether the Fed sounds more or less concerned about inflation and the need for further rate increases. Three possible scenarios for Bitcoin and crypto Scenario 1: Expected outcome - The Fed holds rates and remains cautious The Fed leaves interest rates unchanged and signals that another increase in December is still likely. Because markets already expect this, the decision might not provide Bitcoin with a strong reason to rise or fall. Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin remains choppy and directionless, with buyers and sellers continuing to compete around $80,000. Altcoins may also struggle to establish a convincing recovery. For our tradeCompass, Bitcoin remaining between $79,870 and $80,860 would favor patience rather than forcing a directional trade. Scenario 2: Bullish surprise - The Fed signals fewer rate increases The Fed leaves rates unchanged but unexpectedly suggests that inflation is becoming less concerning, making another rate increase in December less certain. This would be meaningful because investors expecting higher interest rates might suddenly reconsider their outlook. Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin rallies as investors become more willing to take risks. Ethereum and other cryptocurrencies could also benefit, particularly if the US dollar and bond yields decline. For our tradeCompass, a sustained break above $80,860 would bring the bullish targets into focus, starting at $81,770, followed by $85,200. Scenario 3: Bearish surprise - The Fed raises rates or warns of more hikes The Fed unexpectedly increases interest rates immediately, or leaves them unchanged but suggests that inflation is serious enough to require several additional increases. This would be a more aggressive message than markets currently expect. Possible crypto reaction: Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could sell off sharply as investors reduce exposure to riskier assets. A stronger US dollar and rising bond yields could add pressure. For our tradeCompass, a sustained move below $79,870 would activate the bearish scenario, with initial targets at $79,630 and $79,310. If selling continues, the lower targets become relevant. What should Bitcoin traders watch? The Fed decision is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. New York time on Wednesday, followed by the press conference at 2:30 p.m. Traders can also watch the US dollar and Treasury yields for clues about how financial markets interpret the announcement. And there is another potential catalyst on Thursday, October 29, when important US inflation (PCE) and economic growth (GDP) figures are scheduled for release. The important lesson: Markets respond to surprises, not simply whether news sounds good or bad. Even a decision to do nothing can move Bitcoin if the Fed's message changes what investors expect next. That is another reason to use the tradeCompass as a conditional trading map, rather than trying to predict the Fed's decision or Bitcoin's immediate reaction. Educational only. Trade at your own risk. Cryptocurrency markets can be highly volatile, and losses may exceed expectations when trading with leverage. This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.
